newsitem.title: USA: Amtrak train derails in N.J., drawbridge suspect.
newsitem.headline: Amtrak train derails in N.J., drawbridge suspect.

text.p: An Amtrak passenger train travelling from Washington to Boston derailed and plunged down an embankment into a marsh on Saturday, but there were no serious injuries.

At least 88 passengers and three crew members were on board when the accident occurred near the Hackensack River drawbridge, about 6 miles west of New York City, Amtrak spokeswoman Isabel Kaldenbach said.

About 35 passengers were taken to hospitals and all were treated and released, Kaldenbach said. Two others, both Amtrak employees, remained in a hospital for observation but they were expected to be released on Sunday, she said.

Sen. Frank Lautenberg of New Jersey told reporters at the scene that the derailment may have been caused by a drawbridge that left an improper alignment of the track. "The track did not connect as it should," he said.
National Transportation Safety Board investigators will look into the operation of the drawbridge as a possible cause of the derailment, NTSB spokesman Peter Goelz told Reuters.

"We are going to be looking into the operation of the drawbirdge. We understand that there were some difficulties with the drawbridge early this morning and that certainly is going to be one of the important areas," he said.
The train was unreserved and passengers can buy tickets on board so it was not known how many passengers there were.
Six cars of the 14-car train came off the track in the 6:33 a.m. EST derailment, including two locomotives, one mail car and three passenger cars.

A second passenger train, The Carolinian, southbound for Charlotte, N.C., from New York City was sideswiped by the careening cars of the derailed train as it went by on the adjacent track, but no one was injured on that train, the spokeswoman said.

The southbound train was held up for several hours before it went on to Newark, N.J., where passengers were transferred to other trains, she said. Service between Newark and New York on Amtrak's busiest line was disrupted for most of Saturday.
"We expect to have one track back in service late Saturday and a second track in service by Monday morning," the spokeswoman said.

A spokeswoman for New Jersey Transit, Penny Hackett, said Amtrak was stopping trains in Philadelphia to combine them and send them on to Newark, where passengers were being transferred by bus to New York City to resume their travel.
